questions.title: Clindamycin carries a C difficile diarrhea risk to counsel on discharge
questions.question: A patient is being discharged from the hospital on a 3-week course of clindamycin. Which of the following potential adverse effects should be discussed with her?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension) is classically linked to agents such as tetracyclines or vitamin A excess, not clindamycin.
explanations.B: Correct. Clindamycin carries a well-recognised risk of Clostridium difficile diarrhea, including its severe form, pseudomembranous colitis, because it disrupts normal gut flora and allows C. difficile to overgrow -- a risk significant enough that any patient discharged on a multi-week clindamycin course should be specifically counselled about it. Pseudotumor cerebri, hyperbilirubinemia and nephrotoxicity are not clindamycin's characteristic adverse effects.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hyperbilirubinemia is not a characteristic clindamycin adverse effect.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Nephrotoxicity is a concern with drugs such as aminoglycosides, not a characteristic clindamycin adverse effect.

questions.learning_objective: State that Clostridium difficile diarrhea is a clindamycin adverse effect that should be discussed with a patient discharged on a multi-week course.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Clostridium difficile diarrhea."

questions.title: Vancomycin is not a macrolide
questions.question: All of them belongs to macrolides EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Correct (as the EXCEPT). Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis, not a macrolide. Azithromycin, erythromycin and clarithromycin are the true macrolides among the options, sharing the class's characteristic 50S-ribosomal-subunit-binding mechanism, which vancomycin does not share.
explanations.B: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- azithromycin is a genuine macrolide.
explanations.C: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- erythromycin is a genuine macrolide, the class's prototype member.
explanations.D: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- clarithromycin is a genuine macrolide.

questions.learning_objective: Identify vancomycin as a glycopeptide, not a macrolide, distinguishing it from azithromycin, erythromycin and clarithromycin.

questions.title: Aminoglycosides are mainly effective against aerobic, not anaerobic, gram-negative bacteria
questions.question: Concerning Aminoglycosides, the following are true except:

options.A: They cause concentration-dependant not time -dependent bacterial killing
options.B: They are mainly effective in anaerobic gram negative bacteria
options.C: They have synergistic antimicrobial effects with beta-lactams
options.D: Their doses should be adjusted according to creatinine clearance

explanations.A: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- this statement is true. Aminoglycosides show concentration-dependent killing, so their efficacy tracks peak drug levels rather than the duration of time above the MIC.
explanations.B: Correct (as the EXCEPT). Aminoglycosides require oxygen-dependent active transport to cross the bacterial cell membrane and reach their ribosomal target, so they are mainly effective against aerobic, not anaerobic, gram-negative bacteria. Anaerobic organisms lack the oxidative transport process aminoglycoside uptake depends on, making this statement the false one among the options.
explanations.C: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- this statement is true. Aminoglycosides act synergistically with beta-lactams, since beta-lactam-induced cell wall damage improves aminoglycoside penetration into the bacterial cell.
explanations.D: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- this statement is true. Aminoglycosides are renally cleared and nephrotoxic, so doses are adjusted according to creatinine clearance.

questions.learning_objective: State that aminoglycosides are mainly effective against aerobic, not anaerobic, gram-negative bacteria, because their uptake requires oxygen-dependent active transport.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: They are mainly effective in anaerobic gram negative bacteria"

questions.title: Macrolides are 50S-subunit inhibitors that are bacteriostatic
questions.question: Macrolids are -------- ribosomal subunit inhibitors that are ---------.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Macrolides target the 50S subunit, not the 30S subunit, and are bacteriostatic, not bactericidal.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Macrolides are bacteriostatic, not bactericidal, even though they correctly target the 50S subunit.
explanations.C: Correct. Macrolides (erythromycin, azithromycin, clarithromycin) bind the bacterial ribosome's 50S subunit, blocking translocation during protein synthesis. This inhibition is bacteriostatic rather than bactericidal. This distinguishes macrolides from 30S-targeting classes such as aminoglycosides and tetracyclines, and from bactericidal protein synthesis inhibitors.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Macrolides target the 50S subunit, not the 30S subunit, even though they are correctly described as bacteriostatic.

questions.learning_objective: State that macrolides are 50S-ribosomal-subunit-targeting, bacteriostatic protein synthesis inhibitors.

questions.title: Erythromycin is used safely in pregnancy
questions.question: Which of the following is used safely in pregnancy?

explanations.A: Correct. Erythromycin is generally considered safe for use in pregnancy and is a standard alternative when a pregnant patient needs treatment but cannot receive drug classes that carry recognised fetal risk. Doxycycline (a tetracycline) causes fetal teeth discolouration and bone growth disturbance, moxifloxacin (a fluoroquinolone) carries a risk to developing cartilage, and gentamicin (an aminoglycoside) risks fetal ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity -- none of the other three is the safe choice this question asks for.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Doxycycline is a tetracycline, a class avoided in pregnancy because of fetal teeth discolouration and bone growth disturbance.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Moxifloxacin is a fluoroquinolone, a class generally avoided in pregnancy because of a risk to developing fetal cartilage.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside, a class avoided in pregnancy because of a risk of fetal ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.

questions.learning_objective: Identify erythromycin as safe to use in pregnancy, unlike doxycycline, moxifloxacin or gentamicin.

questions.title: Clindamycin and erythromycin antagonise each other at a shared ribosomal site
questions.question: Which of the following antibiotic combinations is inappropriate based on antagonism at the same site of action?

explanations.A: Correct. Clindamycin and erythromycin both bind overlapping sites on the bacterial ribosome's 50S subunit, so combining them is antagonistic -- one drug can displace or block the other's binding, reducing the combination's net antibacterial effect compared with either drug given alone. Ciprofloxacin/amoxicillin, tigecycline/azithromycin and doxycycline/amoxicillin do not share this same-site 50S antagonism.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ciprofloxacin (a DNA gyrase inhibitor) and amoxicillin (a cell-wall inhibitor) act at entirely different sites, so this combination is not the same-site antagonism the question asks for.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Tigecycline and azithromycin both target the ribosome but do not share clindamycin/erythromycin's specific overlapping 50S binding-site antagonism.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Doxycycline (a 30S-subunit inhibitor) and amoxicillin (a cell-wall inhibitor) act at different sites, so this combination is not the same-site antagonism the question asks for.

questions.learning_objective: State that clindamycin and erythromycin are antagonistic when combined, since both bind an overlapping site on the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Clindamycin and erythromycin."
